composio.note: Composio lists ServiceNow under 'Bring your own OAuth app'. Create the auth config with your own client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow, so you must register an OAuth client and supply its client ID and secret in a custom auth config.
reasons: No Composio-managed app exists for ServiceNow
Managed apps elsewhere share quota and show 'Composio wants to access your account'
Your own app gives dedicated quota and your own scopes

prerequisites.title: Admin role on a ServiceNow instance

prerequisites.title: Valid CA-signed certificate

steps.title: Get admin access to an instance
steps.detail: You or the customer's admin needs the security_admin or oauth_admin role on the instance.
steps.done_when: You can open System OAuth > Application Registry.

steps.title: Create OAuth client in Application Registry
steps.detail: The instance auto-generates the client ID. Set the grant type to Authorization Code and define each scope separately.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are recorded.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config via API
steps.detail: Use the client ID and secret, and take the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard. Check that it matches the registry record.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists for the servicenow toolkit.

steps.title: Repeat registration per customer instance
steps.detail: Each customer's admin registers the client in their own instance. Whether one auth config can serve many instances is not confirmed.

steps.title: Prepare Store certification package
steps.detail: Draft listing content and a submission checklist for the Store.

steps.title: Submit app for certification
steps.detail: Submit through the ServiceNow app publisher process.

steps.title: Wait for certification
steps.detail: Typically 3-5 weeks, depending on app size and iteration speed.

traps.title: Third-party access tokens have a 30-day lifespan
traps.detail: Third-party access tokens have a 30-day lifespan.

traps.title: Third-party refresh tokens have a 365-day lifespan
traps.detail: Third-party refresh tokens have a 365-day lifespan.

traps.title: No managed app in Composio
traps.detail: Without your own client ID and secret you cannot connect ServiceNow at all.

traps.title: Instance token lifetimes
traps.detail: Access tokens last 30 minutes and refresh tokens 100 days by default when the instance is the provider. Plan for refresh and re-consent.

traps.title: Self-signed certificates fail
traps.detail: The OAuth client will not connect to endpoints using self-signed certificates.

traps.title: Recertification after changes
traps.detail: Store apps can need recertification for new releases and code changes.

blockers.symptom: Cannot see System OAuth > Application Registry
blockers.what_it_means: Your user lacks the required OAuth admin role.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the instance admin for security_admin or oauth_admin.

evidence.quote: Composio requests sensible defaults for each toolkit.
evidence.answer: Managed apps request sensible default scopes for each toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still [white-label the Connect Link page](/docs/authentication/white-labeling-authentication#customizing-the-connect-link) with your logo and app title without needing your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Even with a custom auth config, the Connect Link page can be white-labeled with the developer's logo and app title without the developer's own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
evidence.answer: The choice between managed and own credentials can be made per toolkit, and each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: Certification, from design complete and submission for certification to ready for publishing on the store, typically requires 3-5 weeks.
evidence.answer: ServiceNow Store certification (app review plus listing review) typically takes 3-5 weeks from submission to publishing-ready, per a ServiceNow employee post dated 02-14-2023; it can take days or longer than 5 weeks depending on app size and iteration speed.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: In addition to the initial certification, ServiceNow Store apps can require recertification.
evidence.answer: Reviews repeat: Store apps can require recertification for new ServiceNow releases and for code changes, in addition to the initial certification. The page gives no fixed yearly cycle.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: We require you stay current (n-3) with our releases.
evidence.answer: Per a third-party consultancy blog quoting ServiceNow's App Publisher FAQ, publishers must stay within the last three family releases (n-3). This is a secondary report, not the official page.
